lines: GOLDSKIN MINING Co. WORKS. Loading bay, lockers and No. 1 line off this door. Time office off the line. Press hall and assembly beyond it.
The lamp runs are marked in red. All but one of them has been crossed out, and the crossings out are in the same hand as the plan.
SAFETY. No man is to work on the line except in good light.
Under it, in pencil, by somebody who had a rule of his own: they only mind what they can see. Do not work in good light.
CLOCK IN. CLOCK OUT. Cards are to be left in the rack at all times.
Every card in the rack is stamped in for today and not one of them is stamped out. The date is right.
CALL BOXES. Press for a hauler. Do not press twice.
A hauler walks the shortest way it knows to the box that called it. It does not know which of these walls are new.
TIME OFFICE. The stove is in and there is a kettle on the hob. The window onto the yard has been boarded from this side.
The door has no handle on the outside. If it goes badly out there, this is where you will wake.
A glass orb on a kitchen stand, wired into the generator with two lengths of bell wire. The stand is the one from the study at home.
Holding it is like a door handle in winter, and it goes on doing it for a while after you let go.
The orb is clear and the wire is warm. The stand has not moved.
Monday. Had the lamps taken out of No. 1 line, run by run. The men say it is dark and I say it is quieter, and we are both right.
Tuesday. Had the lamps out of the press hall as well. The night man will not walk past the loading bay now, so I have taken his card out of the rack.
Tuesday, later. The generator is warm and I have not started it. There is a glass thing wired into it that nobody ordered and that is on no list I hold.
I have written to the office twice about it. The second letter came back with my own handwriting corrected.
The rest of the diary is sums. Nine, fourteen, nine, fourteen, and then a column that does not add up to anything.
